references.text: The context for the command to maintain the same quota of bricks, even though straw was not given to the Israelites.
Pharaoh repeats the accusation that the Israelites are lazy and demands they make the same amount of bricks.
God's original instruction to Moses to ask Pharaoh to let the people go to sacrifice to the Lord.
Moses and Aaron's request to Pharaoh to let the people of Israel go to hold a festival for the Lord.
Moses and Aaron ask to be allowed to travel three days into the wilderness to sacrifice to the Lord their God.
The background to the Israelites' forced labor in Egypt, including the work with bricks.
The cry of the Israelites to God because of slavery, which God heard.
Direct narrative continuation where Pharaoh's accusation of 'laziness' in 5:17 confirms and reinforces the motivation behind the demand in 5:8.
Complementary account from the same scene showing the consequences of the 'lazy' accusation and the realities of oppression.
Direct continuation of the same command confirming that the logic of oppression (more work without resources) is intensifying.
